**Why the model gave a high‑risk decision**  
The model looks at the information it has and found three key drivers of the 58 % chance of default. First, you have a recent serious delinquency – a payment that was more than 90 days late – which adds the most risk. Second, you currently have 15 open credit lines and loans; having many accounts open also raises the risk. Finally, your monthly income of $16,100 helps a little, but it isn’t enough to offset the other two factors, so the overall risk remains high.

**How you can improve the outlook**  
The model shows three specific actions that could lower the estimated default probability to about 49 %:  
1. Reduce your revolving‑credit utilization (the portion of credit you’re using) from roughly 33 % to 30 %.  
2. Bring your debt‑to‑income ratio down from about 36 % to 30 %.  
3. Close or consolidate some credit accounts so the total number of open lines drops from 15 to around 8.
